newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle markets quiet, $63 passed - trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle markets quiet, $63 passed - trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle feeders continued to pass $63.00 per cwt bids late Wednesday morning, and also passed few $63.50 bids in Kansas, feedlot sources said.
Managers said cattle were priced at $64.00 but despite active packer interest, buyers have yet to raise bids.
"It would buy them all," a Kansas manager said of the $64.00.
Kansas managers said feedlots would break even on cattle at $63.00, while Texas managers said break-even prices may be closer to $64.00.
Kansas sources said buyers from several major packers visited feedlots early Wednesday, but have yet to bid $64.00. One feedlot manager said he also passed a $63.50 bid.
"I've been holding for $64.00 money and I think I will get it," said another Kansas feedlot.
Kansas and Texas feedlot sources said meat packers need cattle and there were several instances of packers taking delivery Wednesday of cattle bought Tuesday.
"They are all short (of cattle), we know that," a feedlot manager said of the meat packers.
